1-311: Evac+Chair Transporter Patient Carrier Seat
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/evac-chair-311-transporter-patient-transport-seat
Manufacturer page: https://evac-chair.com/accessories/patient-carrier-seat/
Spec sheet: Evac+Chair range brochure
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: patient transfer device (200/mo, KD0). Secondary: wheelchair transfer seat (50, KD0), patient transfer seat (0). Ricky's note: the product moves a person from a wheelchair into or out of an Evac+Chair; check the results page, since the term can also bring up lifts and slings.

H1: Evac+Chair Transporter Patient Transfer Device for Wheelchair to Evacuation Chair Transfers – 1-311
Current H1: Evac+Chair 1-311 Transporter Patient Transport Seat
Subtitle: Portable Wheelchair Transfer Seat for Lifting a Person into or out of an Evac+Chair When Self-Transfer Is Difficult
Current subtitle: Evac+Chair 1-311 Transporter Patient Transport Seat
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair Transporter (Evac+Chair calls it the Patient Carrier Seat) is a portable patient transfer device for lifting a person from a wheelchair into an Evac+Chair evacuation chair, or back out of it, when they cannot transfer on their own. A wheelchair cannot be taken down the stairs in an emergency, so the passenger first has to be moved into the evacuation chair, and the Transporter makes that step safer for the passenger and the staff.
The passenger sits in the fabric carrier seat, and staff use the long straps on each side to lift them across from the wheelchair to the evacuation chair. As a wheelchair transfer seat, it keeps the passenger seated and supported during the move, so staff do not have to lift the person under the arms.
Use: Lifts a seated person from a wheelchair into or out of an Evac+Chair evacuation chair, where self-transfer is difficult
Design: Portable fabric carrier seat with long lifting straps on both sides
Compatibility: Made by Evac+Chair for use with Evac+Chair evacuation chairs
Portable: Light and easy to keep with the evacuation chair, so it is ready in an emergency
Available Models and Options
1-311 – Transporter (Patient Carrier Seat): Portable transfer seat for wheelchair to Evac+Chair transfers
[H2] Applications
The Transporter suits any building with an evacuation chair where people who use wheelchairs work, live, study, or visit.
Typical applications include:
Offices, schools, and universities with staff or students who use wheelchairs
Hospitals, clinics, senior living, and care facilities
Hotels, public buildings, and high-rise buildings with an emergency evacuation plan
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
What is a patient transfer device used for?
A patient transfer device helps staff move a person from one seat or surface to another when the person cannot move themselves. The Evac+Chair Transporter is made for one job: moving a person from a wheelchair into an evacuation chair, and back, before and after an evacuation down the stairs.
Why not evacuate a person in their wheelchair?
A wheelchair cannot safely go down the stairs, and elevators should not be used in a fire or power outage. The passenger is moved into an Evac+Chair, which is designed to travel down the stairs, and the Transporter is the patient transfer seat that makes that move easier.
Does the Transporter work with any evacuation chair?
Evac+Chair designed it for transfers into and out of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: the primary keyword "patient transfer device" is in the H1, first sentence, an FAQ question, the meta title, and the meta description. "Wheelchair transfer seat" is in the subtitle and second intro paragraph, and "patient transfer seat" is in an FAQ answer.
Research (Ricky's note): the search results for "patient transfer device" are mostly patents and hospital devices (sheet, winch, and air transfer systems), not evacuation products. So the copy says clearly what this product is for (wheelchair to evacuation chair), and an FAQ explains why a person is moved out of their wheelchair before going down the stairs.
Name: Evac+Chair calls this product the "Patient Carrier Seat." Our page calls it the "1-311 Transporter Patient Transport Seat." I kept our name and mentioned the Evac+Chair name in the first sentence, so it is found either way.
Specs: Evac+Chair publishes only one sentence about this product (no capacity, size, weight, or warranty), and there is no data sheet. A UK store (Safelincs) lists a 160 kg (352 lb) payload, webbing construction, and "a minimum of two users," but that is not from Evac+Chair, so I left it out. Do you have specs from Evac+Chair? The description of the straps and two-person lifting comes from the Evac+Chair product photo.
Duplicate content: our current description is the one Evac+Chair sentence. The new copy is fully rewritten and explains the use case, as Ricky suggested for low-volume pages.
Images: the one current image is the Evac+Chair product photo. Evac+Chair has no other photos of it.
Weight: the variant is set to 20 lbs. Is that the real shipping weight?
Price: $320 with compare-at $427 (75%). No change made.
Current meta description is the general GSA pricing line. GSA is not mentioned in the description, per your note on the other tabs.
